# On Writing Plainly

Good writing is easy to read. Short sentences help. Each one carries a single idea, and the
reader never has to stop and untangle a knot of clauses to find the point.

When a sentence runs long, with clause after clause stacked on top of one another and a great
many subordinate ideas competing for the reader's limited attention all at once, comprehension
falls and the prose begins to feel like work rather than a pleasure to move through.

```python
# code blocks should be ignored by the analysis
def noise():
    return "this text must not count toward the grade or the vocabulary percentage"
```

Use common words. Prefer the plain term over the fancy one. Write the way you talk, and read
your work aloud to hear where it stumbles.
